_comment: Pre-market brief. Regenerated on a schedule and committed; the site only renders it. See tools/market-brief.md for how it is produced and what each field must contain. Everything here is written in our own words from sourced reporting — do not paste licensed article text into this file.
headline: The ten-year touched 5% into the decision. The hike is not the event.
standfirst: Tuesday put every US sector but energy in the red as oil jumped five percent and the 10-year traded through 5.04% for the first time since 2007. A 25bp rise at 14:00 ET is priced at 92–94%; retail sales at 08:30, the dot plot and the 14:30 press conference are where the money is.

bullets.title: The bond market set the tone, and it did so before the Fed said a word
bullets.text: The 10-year rose 5bp to close at 5.00% after touching 5.04%, its highest since July 2007. The 20-year auction cleared at a record 5.42%, the 30-year at 5.36%. The S&P lost 0.45% to 7,585.73, the Dow 0.63% and the Nasdaq 0.78%; the VIX sat at 16.98. Every point on the curve rose together, which is the market saying it is no longer pricing one meeting but a ten-year yield in a world where the Fed hikes into 3.4% inflation.

bullets.title: Oil is the reason, again
bullets.text: WTI jumped 5.1% to $106.56 and Brent 3.3% to $109.17 as fighting intensified in the Middle East; both have given back about one percent this morning. Energy was the only sector to close green, up 2.17%; consumer discretionary was the worst, down 1.75%. Crude is up 23.5% over a month and 81% on the year. This is the channel that produced Friday's hot core CPI, and it has not stopped.

bullets.title: The hike is priced. The projections are not.
bullets.text: CME FedWatch has a 25bp move to 3.75–4.00% at 92–94%, the first rise since July 2023, with roughly a 70% chance of at least one more before year-end. The gap is in the dots: the committee's June median had 3.8% for end-2026 and 3.6% for 2027, while futures sit near 4.18% and 4.55% — close to a full point above the Fed for next year. TD Securities expects the dot plot to show fewer hikes than the market has priced, which would mean knee-jerk dollar weakness at 14:00 before the press conference at 14:30 has its say. Chair Warsh is known to dislike forward guidance, so the dots carry more weight than usual.

bullets.title: Retail sales at 08:30 will look strong, and most of it is petrol
bullets.text: Consensus is +0.8% for August after −0.6% in July, with ex-autos at +0.5%. Gasoline prices rose 3.9% in the month and retail sales are measured in dollars, so the headline is flattered before anyone buys anything. The control group — ex fuel, autos, building materials and food services — is expected at +0.4% after −0.4%, and it is the only line the committee will read six hours before it votes.

bullets.title: The dollar has confirmed, and the UK has already printed
bullets.text: DXY reached 99.60, a two-week high; EUR/USD fell for a fifth straight day to a one-month low near 1.153; USD/JPY sits at 155 with the yen the weakest major. Gold fell to $4,335 in New York before bouncing this morning. UK CPI came in at 3.1% as expected at 06:00 UTC, with core steady at 2.6% and input PPI at 6.1% against 5.4% expected — sterling barely moved, but the market now gives tomorrow's Bank of England a one-in-three chance of hiking rather than the near-certain hold of a week ago.

18:00 UTC. A 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% is 92–94% priced. The dot plot lands at the same instant and is the event.
Historically the larger of the two moves, and frequently the reverse of the 14:00 reaction.
11:00 UTC. A hold at 3.75% is still the base case, but a hike is now priced at one-in-three after today's CPI. The vote split moves sterling.

calendar.note: Four releases in one minute, the morning after an FOMC.
A move to 1.25% remains the base case. The yen is already the weakest major going in.

sessionNote: There are two clean windows today and both are short: after the 08:30 reaction settles and before 14:00, and — for those who trade it — the hour after the press conference ends. Everything else is inside a scheduled event. The 14:00 statement will move price for about a minute before the dots are read; the real move is usually between 14:30 and 15:15, and it frequently reverses the first one. A stop that survives 14:00 has not survived the day.
watchOut: The trap today is trading the decision. A hike priced at 92–94% does not move price when it lands. What moves it is whether the dots show one more hike this year or two, and whether Warsh sounds like a man who intends to keep going — and those two signals can point in different directions within the same half hour. If your rule is to stand aside for scheduled releases, the release today runs from 14:00 to 15:15 ET, not for one minute at 14:00.

archive.headline: Core CPI ran hot into an FOMC that is now 90% priced to hike
archive.summary: Weekend edition. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected, PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year, and September hike odds moved from 61% to about 90%. Equities closed the week higher regardless — S&P +0.86% Friday, VIX −11% — while the 10-year finished at 4.96%.

archive.headline: Core CPI at a four-month high, hike odds jump to ~90%
archive.summary: Headline CPI held at 3.4% year-over-year but core rose 0.3% on the month against 0.2% expected. Energy added 2.1% and gasoline 3.9%; airline fares rose 2.7%. Equities rallied regardless — S&P +0.86%, VIX −11% — while the 10-year touched 4.97%.

archive.headline: PPI beats, ECB hikes to 2.50%
archive.summary: August PPI came in at 5.4% year-over-year against 5.3% expected with July revised up from flat. The ECB raised its deposit rate 25bp to 2.50% effective 16 September and cut its 2028 inflation forecast to 2.1%. September hike odds moved from 61% to 72%.

archive.headline: Oil tops $100, Dow sheds 400 more
archive.summary: Brent broke $100 for the first time since July and the 10-year yield hit a three-year high. Amgen fell over 10% on a failed cardiovascular trial and software names sold off. Barclays nonetheless lifted its year-end S&P target to 7,950.
